headline: Good morning — the RBA has lifted the cash rate to 4.85%, while Wall Street surged after Democrats won Congress in the US midterms.

highlights.label: RBA hikes
highlights.text: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate 25 basis points to 4.85% in a 6-3 split vote, the highest in 18 years.

highlights.label: Wall Street surge
highlights.text: The Dow jumped about 3% and oil fell sharply after Democrats won Congress in the US midterms.

highlights.label: Cyclone Murasu
highlights.text: Andhra Pradesh is assessing damage after Murasu made landfall, and the state has asked the Centre for about Rs 4,500 crore.

tip.title: Take a ten-minute walk after a meal
tip.body: A short, easy walk after lunch or dinner is a simple way to add movement to a desk-bound day. It can also help with digestion and break up long periods of sitting. Even a lap around the block counts.

quote.text: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop.
quote.author: Confucius

items.title: Salesforce to buy voice AI firm Cresta
items.summary: Salesforce has agreed to acquire Cresta, a voice AI company for customer experience, with coverage framing it as a way to add voice agents tied to CRM data. Marketers and service teams should watch how voice interactions feed customer profiles.

items.title: Weekly roundup of new AI martech releases
items.summary: The roundup covers recent launches such as Airship's on-device decisioning AI, Akeneo's product information agents and Canto's digital asset assistant. It shows AI agents spreading across personalisation and content operations. Latest dated items were from late October.

items.title: Building marketing workflows around AI agents
items.summary: A MarTech piece looks at how marketing teams are restructuring workflows around AI agents as teammates. It ties into a MarTech Conference session on the topic held on 4 November.

items.title: Salesforce signs deal to acquire Cresta
items.summary: Salesforce announced a definitive agreement to acquire Cresta, a voice-first customer experience platform, on 2 November. The price was not disclosed by Salesforce; one report puts it at about US$2.7 billion, which is not confirmed by the company.

items.title: Acquisition spree and share price pressure
items.summary: The analysis notes Salesforce continues to buy AI companies despite a weak share price, with the stock reported down about 14% for the year as of 3 November. Execution risk from the pace of deals is flagged as a concern.

items.title: Dreamforce 2026 announcements recap
items.summary: Salesforce's roundup of 21 Dreamforce 2026 announcements includes Koa, described as its first CRM reasoning model for Agentforce. This is older than 48 hours but remains the main product roadmap reference.

items.title: Agentforce Coworker usage climbs sharply
items.summary: The newsroom reports Agentforce Coworker usage rose 21 times in three months, with more than 185,000 users listed. Figures are company-reported and not independently verified.

sfstatus.statusNote: A third-party tracker showed no active Salesforce incidents, with the latest incident resolved on 31 October; status.salesforce.com could not be checked directly.

items.title: No active incidents on Salesforce tracker
items.summary: The tracker, which draws on Salesforce's status page, showed no current incidents and the last one resolved on 31 October. No planned APAC maintenance was found; confirm on status.salesforce.com.

items.title: RBA lifts rates to 18-year high in split vote
items.summary: The Reserve Bank raised the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.85%, its fifth hike this year, with three of nine board members wanting a hold. It adds pressure to mortgage holders and keeps the door open to further increases.

items.title: Wall Street soars after Democrats win midterms
items.summary: US markets rallied sharply after Democrats won the midterm elections, with oil prices dropping. The move matters for Australian shares and fuel costs.

items.title: Minister hopes fuel prices ease after US midterms
items.summary: A federal minister said the government hopes fuel prices will fall following the US midterm outcome. Pump prices remain a cost-of-living pressure alongside higher interest rates.

items.title: Education ministers agree to school system overhaul
items.summary: Education ministers have agreed to what ABC describes as the biggest shake-up of the school system in years. Details were not confirmed in the summary reviewed.

items.title: Meta lets Australians opt out of AI training
items.summary: Australians can now opt out of Meta using their Facebook and Instagram data to train its AI. The change is relevant to privacy and to marketers using Meta platforms.

items.title: Cabinet clears Rs 14,500 crore energy storage scheme
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh of grid-scale storage on 4 November, reported at Rs 14,500 crore (one outlet cites a different figure). It supports grid reliability and renewable integration.

items.title: Andhra seeks Rs 4,500 crore Centre aid after cyclones
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh asked the Centre for about Rs 4,500 crore in immediate relief after cyclones Arnab and Murasu. Figures are the state's own estimates.

items.title: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall on Andhra coast
items.summary: The severe cyclone made landfall, uprooting trees, toppling power poles and flooding low-lying areas, with heavy damage reported in Prakasam and Bapatla. Early reports indicated no deaths or injuries.

items.title: State seeks Rs 4,500 crore immediate relief
items.summary: Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu requested central aid, citing crop damage across about 52,500 hectares. The loss figures are the state government's own estimates.

items.title: Modi phones Naidu on cyclone relief
items.summary: The Prime Minister called Naidu on 4 November to ask about the damage and praised relief efforts. It signals central backing for the state's request.

items.title: Flights cancelled and schools shut before landfall
items.summary: Ahead of landfall, 19 flights were cancelled, schools closed in seven districts and Rs 37 crore was released to 17 districts. The measures aimed to limit casualties.

items.title: Stocks surge and oil collapses after Democrats sweep midterms
items.summary: US stocks rallied strongly on 4 November as oil fell sharply following the midterm results. Index levels are from secondary reports and may differ slightly from official closes.

items.title: Dow's best day since April 2025
items.summary: The Dow reportedly gained 1,569 points, its biggest daily gain since April 2025, while gold moved back above US$4,000 an ounce. Not independently confirmed.

items.title: ASX 200 slides as miners sell off before US result
items.summary: The ASX 200 closed lower on Wednesday, led by materials and defence stocks, ahead of the US election outcome. Selling was linked to worries about tighter AI oversight.

items.title: RBA's fifth hike weighs on shares and the dollar
items.summary: The RBA lifted the cash rate to 4.85% in a 6-3 split vote, with AUD/USD reported below 0.70. The next decision is on 8 December.

items.title: Futures point higher after Wall Street rally
items.summary: ABC's live blog reported ASX 200 futures around 9,027 after US markets rallied. Not independently confirmed.

items.title: Home values fall 1.2% in October, seventh straight drop
items.summary: Cotality's index shows national values fell 1.2% in October, with Sydney down 1.6% and Melbourne down 0.8%. Melbourne values are about 7.6% lower than a year ago.

items.title: Downturn lands just before RBA hike
items.summary: Cotality described the fall as the fastest downturn pace in 40 years. The RBA then lifted the cash rate to 4.85% on 3 November.

items.title: RBA hike to hit mortgage holders
items.summary: The cash rate is now at its highest in 18 years after a fifth hike this year. Higher repayments add pressure to an already falling market.

items.title: Auction clearance rates weak in October
items.summary: Capital city clearance rates averaged 45.2% during October, with Melbourne near an 18-year low for a week before a rebound later in the month. Figures come from different weeks and sources.
